Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of the same problem. Each time the function runs, it works on a reduced input until it reaches a simple case that can be answered directly—this is called the **base case**. By combining the results of each smaller call, the original problem is solved step by step. Think of it like a set of nested Russian dolls: you open one doll (call), find a smaller doll inside (next call), and continue until you reach the tiniest doll (base case), then you close them back up in reverse order.
